name: Bloomberg

Software Engineer.dsaDepth: Heavy - 2–3 coding rounds (LeetCode medium–hard: graphs, trees, intervals) drawn heavily from Bloomberg’s own tagged question pool
rounds: Recruiter screen (~30 min, motivation and background, no technical questions)
Technical phone screen (~45 min, 1 coding problem from Bloomberg’s well-known tagged list)

Superday: 2–3 coding rounds (medium–hard: BFS/graph variants, topological sort, intervals), a system/low-level design round (e.g. portfolio management service, URL shortener, key-value store), and a resume deep-dive
Engineering manager round: project discussion, team fit
extraTopics: Sustained follow-up pressure after a working solution - defending trade-offs matters as much as reaching an answer
Genuine interest in Bloomberg/fintech ("why Bloomberg" is asked repeatedly across rounds)

Senior Software Engineer.dsaDepth: Heavy - same coding bar, system design round widely reported as the hardest part of the loop
rounds: Similar structure to entry-level, with system design weighted more heavily and deeper resume/leadership discussion
extraTopics: Leading design discussions and justifying architecture choices

ladder.title: Software Engineer
ladder.notes: No public numbered-level scheme found; titles are Software Engineer -> Senior -> Lead

rolesNotes: Bloomberg does not publish numbered levels the way Google/Amazon/Meta do; the ladder here is inferred from title progression in candidate reports, not a confirmed official scheme. The interview-loop detail itself is well corroborated across multiple independent sources.
